claims.text: USGS recorded a magnitude 6.8 earthquake on 28 July 2026 at 07:27:15 UTC, 5 km E of Uto, Japan (32.6817N, 130.7217E), at a depth of approximately 10 km.

GDACS's earthquake report (event 1554552) for this M6.8 Kumamoto earthquake assesses an Orange alert ("this earthquake can have a medium humanitarian impact based on the magnitude and the affected population and their vulnerability"), with an exposed population of about 1.2 million people at MMI VII or greater. No confirmed casualty figure is given.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: USGS's PAGER product for event us6000tgb9 remains unchanged (Red alert, max MMI 9.243, modeled fatality estimates of 724/234, ~1.2 million exposed to MMI VII+). The event page additionally lists a Red liquefaction hazard alert (~240,000 people exposed) and an Orange landslide hazard alert (~2,800 people exposed) -- hazard-model layers not previously reflected in this record. No allowlisted source has yet published a confirmed casualty or damage figure as of 10 August 2026.

claims.text: FDMA Report No. 54 (16 August 2026, 10:00 JST): the national death toll remains 39 and injured/missing figures are unchanged (397 injured nationally, 27 missing); housing damage assessments continued to rise between Report No. 51 (13 Aug) and No. 54 (16 Aug) -- total collapse 1,274 to 1,287 units, half collapse 1,046 to 1,185 units, and total damaged-housing units 11,796 to 13,952 -- reflecting ongoing survey completion. As of 14 August 17:00, further prefectural Emergency Fire Response Team reinforcements (from Fukuoka, Saga, Oita, Miyazaki and Kagoshima) withdrew; Kumamoto Prefecture's disaster response headquarters, established 28 July, remains active.

claims.source_name: Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA)
claims.text: FDMA Disaster Report No. 57 (19 August 2026, 10:00 JST), successfully read after two consecutive days of PDF-parsing failures on Reports No. 55/56: confirmed national death toll unchanged at 39 (Kumamoto Prefecture breakdown: Yatsushiro City 20, Uto City 3, Kashima Town 7, Kosa Town 1, Hikawa Town 5, plus 1 possible disaster-related death from worsened injury/physical strain and 2 deaths still under investigation for relation to the disaster). Nationally, 0 people remain listed as missing in this report's table (down from 27 missing reported around Report No. 54, 16 August). Injured total nationally is 401 (28 severely injured, 334 lightly/minor injured, subtotal 362 injured, plus the 39 deaths). Housing damage rose to 16,634 total buildings damaged (1,515 fully destroyed, 1,530 half destroyed, 13,589 partially damaged) -- up sharply from 13,952 total damaged as of Report No. 54 (16 August) as damage assessment surveys continue. Evacuation instructions (hinan shiji) now cover 2 cities and 1 town in Kumamoto Prefecture, 45,667 households / 100,970 people -- down from 3 municipalities / 103,922 households / 219,027 people as of Report No. 54, a roughly 54% reduction in the population under evacuation order. Prefectural Emergency Fire Response Team reinforcements were further withdrawn on 14 August 17:00 (the Fukuoka overall-command unit, the Fukuoka/Kitakyushu command-support units, and the Fukuoka/Saga/Oita/Miyazaki/Kagoshima prefectural units); Kumamoto Prefecture's disaster response headquarters, established 28 July, remains active. On 16 August, Japan's Minister of Internal Affairs and Communications and the FDMA Commissioner visited the disaster area, meeting Kumamoto's governor and Uki City's mayor and thanking fire personnel.

USGS's PAGER population-exposure estimate for this earthquake found about 1,422,182 people exposed to MMI VII (Very Strong) shaking or greater and about 8,057,091 additional people exposed to MMI V (Moderate) shaking, almost entirely within Japan (a small population of about 65 people in South Korea was exposed to MMI III, weak, shaking).

claims.text: FDMA Disaster Report No. 59 (21 August 2026, 10:00 JST): the national confirmed death toll was revised down to 38 (from 39) after one of two deaths previously listed as still under investigation for relation to the disaster was judged unrelated and withdrawn from the count; missing remains 0 nationally, and injured remains unchanged at 364 (30 severely, 334 minor). Housing damage assessments rose to 21,033 buildings damaged in total (1,589 fully destroyed, 1,950 half destroyed, 17,494 partially damaged), up from 16,634 in Report No. 57. Evacuation instructions narrowed further to a single municipality in Kumamoto Prefecture covering 25,314 households and 56,006 people, down from 29,437 households and 65,014 people in Report No. 58, with the stronger Emergency Safety Confirmation category now at zero.

USGS PAGER's loss-model data, updated 29 July 2026, records a maximum shaking intensity of MMI IX, a fatality alert level of Orange (gvalue 1.77, up from Yellow) and an economic alert level of Red (gvalue 2.28). Aggregated population exposure at MMI VII or greater is about 1,236,912 (374,783 at MMI VII + 635,782 at MMI VIII + 226,347 at MMI IX). PAGER's empirical loss model estimates 724 total fatalities (0 in South Korea) and $12,724,898,845 in economic losses; PAGER's semi-empirical structural model separately estimates 234 fatalities. These are automated probabilistic model outputs, not confirmed casualty or damage figures.

description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck southern Kumamoto Prefecture, Kyushu, Japan, on 28 July 2026, centred 5 km east of Uto City at a depth of about 10 km. Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA) confirms 38 deaths and 364 injured, with no one now listed as missing nationally, and damage surveys have raised the building total to 21,033 (1,589 fully destroyed); evacuation instructions have been narrowed further to a single municipality in Kumamoto Prefecture, covering 25,314 households and 56,006 people. Water outages, which peaked at about 108,100 households, have been cut to about 27,800, with full restoration targeted by the end of August; the Kyushu Expressway has reopened to general vehicles, while the Kyushu Shinkansen and two local rail lines remain suspended. USGS's PAGER product retains a Red alert and GDACS an Orange alert, with about 1.2 million people exposed to MMI VII or greater shaking.

impact.summary: FDMA Report No. 59 (21 August 2026) confirms 38 deaths -- revised down from 39 after one previously unresolved case was judged unrelated to the disaster -- and 364 injured (30 severely), with no one listed as missing nationally. Housing damage assessments have risen to 21,033 buildings (1,589 fully destroyed). Evacuation instructions have been narrowed further to a single municipality in Kumamoto Prefecture -- 25,314 households and 56,006 people -- down from 29,437 households and 65,014 people the day before. MLIT reports water outages reduced to about 27,800 households from a peak of about 108,100, and the Kyushu Expressway reopened to general vehicles while the Kyushu Shinkansen remains suspended. USGS's PAGER product retains a Red alert (maximum MMI 9.243) and GDACS an Orange alert, with about 1.2 million people exposed to MMI VII or greater shaking.

FDMA Report No. 58 held the death toll at 39 with no one still listed as missing; the national injured total rose slightly to 364 (30 severely injured, up from 28), and evacuation instructions were narrowed further to a single municipality covering 29,437 households / 65,014 people, down from 45,667 households / 100,970 people.

FDMA Report No. 57 held the death toll at 39 and put the national injured total at 401, with no one still listed as missing, down from 27; damage surveys raised the building total to 16,634 (1,515 fully destroyed, 1,530 half destroyed, 13,589 partially damaged), and evacuation instructions were narrowed to two cities and one town covering 45,667 households / 100,970 people.

FDMA Report No. 52 put building damage at 12,367 in total (1,275 fully destroyed, 1,088 half destroyed) with 358 injured; per MLIT Report No. 40, water outages fell to about 27,800 households and the Kyushu Expressway reopened to general vehicles system-wide for the first time since the quake, one section remaining under alternating one-lane control.

FDMA Report No. 51 showed damage assessments still rising, with 1,274 buildings fully destroyed and about 11,796 damaged in total and deaths unchanged at 39; MLIT Report No. 39 showed water outages cut from a peak of about 108,100 households to about 28,400 across three Kumamoto municipalities, with full restoration targeted by the end of August.

FDMA Report No. 50 confirmed a death toll of 39 — the first official confirmed casualty figure for this event, superseding USGS PAGER's automated model estimates — with 1,252 buildings fully destroyed and 11,240 damaged in total; the toll had been stable since around Report No. 34 (8 August). MLIT Report No. 38 reported the Kyushu Expressway reopened to emergency vehicles system-wide, with water outages persisting in 15 municipalities across 4 prefectures.
USGS's event page added a Red liquefaction hazard alert (about 240,000 people exposed) and an Orange landslide hazard alert (about 2,800 people exposed) alongside the existing PAGER alerts.
GDACS published an earthquake report for the event (id 1554552), assessing an Orange alert for medium humanitarian impact with about 1.2 million people exposed to MMI VII or greater shaking.

USGS's PAGER loss-model update raised the maximum estimated shaking intensity to MMI IX and the fatality alert from Yellow to Orange, with the economic-loss alert remaining Red; the empirical model estimated 724 fatalities and the semi-empirical structural model 234, as automated probabilistic estimates rather than confirmed figures.
